about.p1: I am Nerea Wenting Llugany Montoya. I specialize in 3D and 2D animation, motion graphics and graphic design, and I develop game assets ready for Unity & Unreal.

process.title: From concept to engine-ready assets
process.desc: A structured pipeline designed to bridge the gap between creative vision and technical implementation in Unity or Unreal.

1.title: Discovery & Briefing
1.desc: We define the scope, technical constraints, and artistic goals. I analyze your existing pipeline to ensure my assets fit perfectly.

2.title: Art Direction & Concepts
2.desc: I create moodboards, sketches, or style frames to align on the visual direction before moving into expensive production phases.

3.title: Prototyping & Blocking
3.desc: For 3D/Games, I create greybox models or rough animations to test timing and functionality within the engine immediately.

4.title: Production & Animation
4.desc: The heavy lifting. Modeling, texturing, rigging, and animating. I focus on clean topology and optimized performance.

5.title: Technical Integration
5.desc: I import assets into the engine, setting up materials, prefabs, animation controllers, and particle systems.

6.title: Polish & Handover
6.desc: Final optimization, bug fixing, and file organization. I deliver a clean package ready for your developers to use.

thorny.title: Thorny Seasons
thorny.desc: A 2D platformer developed in Unity (C#). Features custom physics, a persistent data economy system, and a Finite State Machine (FSM) boss battle.

monsters.title: Monsters, Inc.
monsters.desc: A technical sound redesign using Reaper. Demonstrates the complete foley process, recording custom textures and mixing them with EQ and Reverb.

vincent.title: Vincent's Journey
vincent.desc: A specialized 3D animation showcase using Blender and Rigify. Explores body mechanics by applying three distinct emotional states to a walk cycle.

banana.title: Operation Banana
banana.desc: A character animation study utilizing Adobe Animate. Showcases the technical challenges of a weighted walk cycle and phoneme-based lip-syncing.

faq.q1: What tools and tech did you use?
faq.a1: Each project lists the exact stack (e.g., Unity, Blender, After Effects, C#) and delivered formats (playable build, MP4, FBX). If you would like to know exactly which tools or tools I know, you can go to the About page to learn more.
faq.q2: Which projects are most relevant to my needs?
faq.a2: You can quickly find the most relevant work by using the category filters at the top of the page: Design, Animation, Games, Web/Apps and Audio. Each case study also includes a short 1-line outcome, so you can instantly identify the ones that match your goals. If you're unsure, feel free to contact me about what you're looking for and I'll point you to the best examples.
faq.q3: What problem were you solving and what was your approach?
faq.a3: Each case study follows: Problem → Constraints → Approach → Deliverables → Results. I include key decisions and a short visual process (wireframes, before/after).
faq.a4: My usual process: brief → research & reference gathering → prototype or draft → feedback & iteration → final delivery + hand-over + documentation. I keep you involved at every step, so you always know what's going on.
faq.q5: How often do you update the portfolio?
faq.a5: I refresh the portfolio quarterly and add significant new case studies as they finish, so the site reflects my current skills and availability.
faq.q6: Do you follow coding / design best practices (version control, consistent naming, documentation)?
faq.a6: Yes, for digital or code-based projects I use version control and comment code; for design I organise layers, name elements logically, and keep documentation for deliverables.
